note: The valley's animals (docs/45, steps 1 and 2). Per species: its name, whether it is wild game (renewed at its home up to the cap, and taking every blow and arrow; tame livestock is not renewed and is hurt only on purpose), its walk and run in tiles a second, its body's radius, its health, what it flees and how far (null: it never runs), how far it wanders from its home, how long it stands between walks, how often a stand is spent grazing, what it gives (`yields`: `skin` with a dirk carried, then `butcher`; counts are [least, most] before the weapon's share), and for the boar how it fights back (`fight`). `renew`: one animal back at a wild home below its cap each `seconds` of the game's clock, and never while a player, living or dead, is within `clear` tiles of the home: past the active box (`world.activeTiles`, 40) and the corners of the widest window at the widest zoom (about 39), so nothing materialises in view. `kills`: the share of every yield a kill by each class of weapon leaves (docs/45 section 2: the bow the full yield, a melee weapon less, a halberd ruins it); `classes` names the items whose blows are a class of their own. `work`: the seconds of skinning and butchering. `snare`: a set snare holds a rabbit once `hours` of game time have passed, if a home of rabbits is within `reach` tiles and one of them can be taken unseen. `tracks`: game leaves a print each `every` tiles it goes, kept `seconds` of game time, seen within `radius` tiles of a player (Beastlore 3, open to all until the skills). Defaults, Primary's (docs/45): Michael's to tune.
